title: Obligation of the Other Member to Give Opinion in District Commission Proceedings

content.scenario: In a proceeding before the District Commission, the President and a member differ on a point. The point is referred to another member, but the other member fails to give his opinion within one month. The consumer files a petition in the High Court to direct the other member to give his opinion.
content.outcome: The High Court directs the other member to give his opinion on the point referred to him within one month from the date of reference, as mandated by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The High Court also clarifies that the opinion of the majority shall be the order of the District Commission.

user_queries: What is the obligation of the other member in District Commission proceedings?
Can a member be directed to give his opinion within a specified time?
What is the role of the High Court in ensuring compliance with the Consumer Protection Act?
